subject: Term cadence guardrails + procurement signoff (auto-renew exceptions)
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@stratusdata.com
Date: 2025-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stratus MSA redline and term questions

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is our current redline of Redwood's MSA (Stratus_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf). A couple of items our procurement team flagged where we could use clarity before we proceed to signatures: 

- Auto-renew mechanics: can you confirm whether renewals are automatic for 12-month increments and whether Redwood will send a renewal notice 30 days before?
- Notice window: we asked for a 30-day termination notice for pilots but the MSA is written for 60/90 days; is that negotiable?
- Termination for convenience: Stratus wants the option to exit with a pro-rated refund; our legal is proposing a 30% early-exit fee if cancelled before 12 months.

We looped in our legal mailbox for redline comments. Can your procurement/legal team advise on realistic guardrails here? Happy to hop on a short call if that's easier.

Attachments: Stratus_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Procurement
Stratus Data
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus MSA redline and term questions

Hi Elaine —

Appreciate the redline and the clear asks. Quick summary from my side so we have alignment before legal starts deep redlines: 

1) Auto-renew: Our standard is 12-month auto-renew by default. We typically provide a 30-day renewal notice by email for enterprise deals, but that notice is contractual (we're open to putting a specific notice cadence in the order form).
2) Notice windows: For pilot agreements we can consider shortening to 30 days; for enterprise commitments we request 60–90 days depending on the TCV and any volume commitments.
3) Termination for convenience: We don't usually offer unconstrained pro-rated refunds. A pragmatic compromise is a structured early-exit schedule tied to remaining committed months (e.g., capped fee equal to up to 3 months of committed spend for pilots, scaled to 3–6 months for larger orders).

Next steps I propose: 
- Vanessa (procurement) to confirm what level of flexibility we can give operationally and whether an 'early exit ladder' makes sense here.
- Karthik (legal) to propose specific redline language we can send back to Stratus.
- Elaine, if you can call out the scenarios (pilot vs enterprise) in the redline, that will speed things up.

I'll follow up with a short internal note to legal/procurement. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute sync to finalize the order form language.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-10T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus MSA redline and term questions — procurement view

Thanks Michael & Elaine. Quick procurement read: 

- For pilots under $25k MRR equivalent, 30-day notice is operationally acceptable. We will treat pilots as "on-demand" with shorter offboarding SLAs.
- For Commercial/Enterprise orders, we need 60–90 day notice to coordinate capacity teardown and invoice cleanups; 90 days if there are reserved/dedicated pools.
- On termination-for-convenience fees: recommend an explicit ladder instead of a flat percentage — e.g.:
  * Cancellation within month 0–3: refund less 90% of remaining committed fees
  * Month 4–6: refund less 50%
  * After month 6: refund less 25%
  This gives Stratus predictability and covers Redwood's ramp costs.

Attached is a practical ops checklist I'm proposing for the order form (termination-ops-checklist.xlsx) — covers data export windows, access revocation timelines, and who owns the migration runbook.

Elaine — can you confirm which bucket Stratus expects to fall into and whether the ladder above is acceptable as a starting point? Also copying Laura for finance ingestion issues (prepaid credits, refunds).

Procurement note: we'll need signoff from finance on the refund mechanics before agreeing.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-11T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus MSA redline and term questions — legal recommended language

Elaine / team —

Thanks for the redline. High-level legal guidance and draft language suggestions below for the Term / Auto-Renew / Termination for Convenience sections: 

1) Term and Renewal: "The Initial Term shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for twelve (12) months. Thereafter, the Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term for Pilot Agreements or at least ninety (90) days for Enterprise Agreements."

2) Notice mechanics: include an explicit delivery mechanism: "Notice shall be deemed given when sent to the notice email addresses listed in the Order Form or executed via DocuSign link and receipt is acknowledged."

3) Termination for Convenience: provide a capped ladder: "Customer may terminate for convenience upon payment of a termination fee equal to the sum of: (a) the remaining monthly recurring fees for up to six (6) months, or (b) the remaining prepaid balance, whichever is less; plus reasonable transition assistance costs not to exceed $25,000, unless otherwise agreed in the Order Form."

4) Data/export SLA on termination: require a 30-day export window for pilots and a 90-day export window for enterprise with specific transfer methods called out in the termination-ops-checklist.

Please note: the termination fee cap is designed to limit Redwood's exposure while giving Stratus a predictable cost to exit. If Stratus insists on pro-rata refunds without any fee, we will need additional commercial concessions (e.g., non-refundable onboarding fee, reduced discount).

I'll prepare tracked redline language and circulate a one-page summary for exec review. Also sharing a DocuSign stub for signature sequencing: https://docusign.com/12345abc

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Michael / Karthik / Vanessa —

Appreciate the concrete options and the draft language. The ladder approach is acceptable in principle. A couple quick asks from Stratus legal before we lock: 

- Can we compress the early termination ladder slightly (e.g., 0–3 months = 75% instead of 90%)? That will make the commercial acceptable to our CFO.
- Please include explicit reference to who pays for data egress (we typically cover reasonable transfer costs but want clarity).

We have a short window this Friday for a 30-minute call to finalize — are you available 10:00–10:30 PT? We're attaching a slim counterproposal for redlines (Stratus_Counter_v2.docx).

If you prefer, I can drop the redline into DocuSign after we confirm the language.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
